questions.question: How does digital inequality affect social justice? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Digital inequality - impacts on social justice -creating unequal access to education -
  • healthcare- employment- government services- information- people from economically weaker
  • sections, rural communities and marginalized groups face greater barriers- bridging the digital
  • divide throug h affordable internet -digital literacy - accessible technology promotes equal
  • opportunities and social inclusion.

questions.question: Analyse the role of CEDAW in prmoting gender equality and protecting womens rights. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• CEDAW-Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women -
  • international treaty promoting gender equality - requires states to eliminate discrimination
  • against women- education, employment, healthcare, politics and family life- encourages legal
  • reforms- equal opportunities- protection against gender-based violence-strengthening women's
  • rights worldwide.

questions.question: Discuss the definition of 'domestic violence' under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 - defines domestic violence
  • broadly to include physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse- also covers threats
  • and harassment - Act protects women in domestic relationships - provides remedies such as
  • protection orders- residence orders- monetary relief- custody orders and compensation.

questions.question: Discuss the major human rights concerns faced by prisoners in India / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Prisoners in India - face several human rights concerns - overcrowding- poor sanitation -
  • inadequate healthcare - custodial violence - torture- insufficient legal assistance - undertrial
  • prisoners may remain incarcerated for long periods - discrimination and limited rehabilitation
  • opportunities-protecting prisoners' dignity requires legal safeguards - prison reforms -
  • accountability and humane treatment.

questions.question: What is “environmental justice”? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Environmental justice- fair distribution of environmental benefits and burdens among all
  • people- regardless of income, caste, gender or ethnicity - ensures equal protection from
  • pollution-access to natural resources - participation in environmental decisions - emphasizes
  • accountability- sustainable development - protection of vulnerable communities from
  • environmental harm.

questions.question: Outline the relationship between human dignity and the constitutional guarantee of Fundamental Rights / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Human dignity- foundation of Fundamental Rights- human beings are end in themselves -
  • guaranteed by the Indian Constitution- various Articles (14-32) protect equality and freedoms-
  • prevents exploitation and humiliation -life with personal liberty - assures the right to li fe with
  • dignity- rights also prevent arbitrary state action and promote justice- autonomy, equality and
  • individual development.

questions.question: Evaluate the role of human rights education in a democratic society. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Human rights education- promotes awareness of fundamental freedoms- equality- justice-
  • democratic values - encourages citizens to respect diversity - challenge discrimination - hold
  • authorities accountable - develop critical thinking and civic responsibility - strengthens
  • democratic participation- human rights education helps prevent abuses - builds an informed,
  • tolerant and inclusive society.

questions.question: Evaluate the role of the UNHCR in protecting and assisting refugees worldwide / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• UNHCR - United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees - protects refugees - asylum
  • seekers- stateless people - provides emergency shelter, food, healthcare, legal assistance -
  • protection from forced return to danger - supports voluntary repatriation - local integration -
  • resettlement- work promotes refugee rights through international cooperation and humanitarian
  • assistance.

questions.question: Explain the significance of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child in shaping the NCPCR's mandate / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• UN Convention on the Rights of the Child - establishes children's rights to survival -
  • development- protection- participation- emphasizes the best interests of the child and
  • protection from exploitation and abuse - NCPCR's mandate reflects these principles -
  • monitoring child -rights laws - investigating violations - reviewing safeguards - recommends
  • measures for effective implementation in India.

questions.question: Briefly explain the human rights concerns associated with displacement caused by development projects. / [CO4] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Development-induced displacement -occurs when people lose homes-land and livelihoods-
  • community networks -because of dams - industries- mines and infrastructure projects - cause
  • poverty, homelessness, cultural loss and inadequate rehabilitation - indigenous communities
  • and vulnerable groups - particularly affected-human rights protection - requires consultation-
  • fair compensation- rehabilitation- livelihood restoration- respect for affected people's dignity.

questions.question: Distinguish between human rights, civil rights and fundamental rights and assess their significance in a democratic polity. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Human rights are universal rights- belonging to every person- Civil rights protect individual
  • freedoms and equal treatment within society - Fundamental Rights are constitutionally
  • guaranteed rights under Part III of the Indian Constitution - Human rights establish universal
  • standards- civil rights ensure social and political equality - Fundamental Rights provide legal
  • remedies against violations- together they promote democracy, justice, liberty, equality, dignity
  • and accountability.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the issues of Refugees and Migrants as a global Human Rights concern. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Refugees and migrants- face major human rights challenges- discrimination- exploitation-
  • trafficking- unsafe journeys - inadequate healthcare - restricted education-Refugees flee
  • persecution or conflict-migrants move for various reasons- non-refoulement protects refugees
  • against forced return to danger- international cooperation- legal protection- humane treatment-
  • access to essential services - protection against exploitation - essential for safeguarding their
  • dignity and rights.

questions.question: Outline the background, objectives and provisions of the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 and assess its human rights implications / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 - enacted to address security challenges in
  • designated disturbed areas- empowers armed forces to maintain public order- including certain
  • search, arrest and force -related powers- Section 4 grants special powers - Section 6 requires
  • prior Central Government sanction for prosecution - critics raise concerns about excessive
  • force- accountability- arbitrary detention- alleged human rights violations.

questions.question: Discuss the specific vulnerabilities faced by women and children during armed conflicts and explain the measures adopted for tgeir protection / [CO4] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Women face sexual violence - trafficking- displacement- gender-based discrimination -
  • Children experience recruitment into armed groups - family separation- injuries-exploitation-
  • disrupted education- international humanitarian law- the Geneva Conventions- the Convention
  • on the Rights of the Child- provide protection-UN Security Council Resolution 1325- addresses
  • women, peace and security-suggested measures- humanitarian assistance- safe shelters- family
  • reunification- rehabilitation- accountability for violations.
